editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall, but a few spots need an editor. In [20] and [23], "sehingga sembilan/enam blok qubit" reads most naturally in Malay as a limit on how many blocks there are. The limit is actually on block size, so it should say "blok sehingga sembilan/enam qubit", the same pattern [22] already uses ("blok 65, 33, dan 27 qubit"). In [24], "Kami dijangka akan meningkatkan" means "we are expected (by others) to increase" rather than "we expect to"; it should be "Kami menjangkakan". "Pass" is rendered two ways: the English "transpiler passes" is used alongside "laluan", sometimes in the same sentence ([4], [13]). Smaller points: "Citation" is translated as "Petikan" ([37], [38]), which means a quoted excerpt. [38] keeps the English word order "`qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package". "kumpulan benang" for thread pool ([25]) is stiff.

examples.source: Currently up to nine qubit blocks.
examples.translation: Pada masa ini sehingga sembilan blok qubit.
examples.suggested: Pada masa ini menyokong blok sehingga sembilan qubit.
examples.why: The Malay word order makes this a limit on how many blocks there are rather than on block size. [23] has the same problem ('sehingga enam blok qubit'), and [22] already uses the correct pattern.

examples.source: We expect to gradually increase the size of the supported blocks.
examples.translation: Kami dijangka akan meningkatkan saiz blok yang disokong secara beransur-ansur.
examples.suggested: Kami menjangkakan saiz blok yang disokong akan ditingkatkan secara beransur-ansur.
examples.why: 'dijangka' is passive and means 'we are expected to'. That moves the expectation from the developers to outside observers.

examples.source: The AI-powered transpiler passes are passes that work as a drop-in replacement...
examples.translation: Transpiler passes berkuasa AI adalah laluan yang berfungsi sebagai pengganti langsung laluan Qiskit...
examples.suggested: Laluan transpiler berkuasa AI ialah laluan yang berfungsi sebagai pengganti langsung...
examples.why: 'pass' appears both as the English 'transpiler passes' and as 'laluan' across the file, even within one sentence. It should be one term throughout.

examples.source: Citation
examples.translation: Petikan
examples.suggested: Sitasi
examples.why: 'Petikan' means a quoted excerpt. For an academic citation, 'Sitasi' or 'Rujukan' is the conventional term.

examples.source: any AI-powered feature from the `qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package
examples.translation: sebarang ciri berkuasa AI daripada `qiskit-ibm-transpiler` package
examples.suggested: sebarang ciri berkuasa AI daripada pakej `qiskit-ibm-transpiler`
examples.why: The English noun and word order were left in place, while [9] correctly uses 'pakej'.

editor_note: Entry 27 is faithful and reads naturally. The trade-off direction is kept intact: 'mengurangkan rep_delay mengurangkan jumlah masa pelaksanaan QPU' comes at the cost of 'kadar ralat penyediaan keadaan yang meningkat'. The 250-mikrosaat default via backend.default_rep_delay is also correct.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The Open Plan caveat in [37], the resilience_level guidance and the PUB description all survive intact. Entry [37] turns the verb "transpile" into the tool noun: "melakukan Transpiler secara tempatan" means "do Transpiler locally" and should read "mentranspil secara tempatan". Entry [16] renders the array-sense "broadcasted" as "disiarkan", which reads like a media broadcast. Entries [9] and [30] use the colloquial "nak" where standard documentation prose would use "ingin" or "hendak".

examples.source: Learn how to transpile locally in the [Transpile](/guides/transpile) section.
examples.translation: Ketahui cara melakukan Transpiler secara tempatan dalam bahagian [Transpile](/guides/transpile).
examples.suggested: Ketahui cara mentranspil secara tempatan dalam bahagian [Transpile](/guides/transpile).
examples.why: The action (transpile) is rendered as the tool noun (Transpiler), so the phrase reads as 'perform Transpiler locally'.

examples.source: the data broadcasted to that circuit
examples.translation: data yang disiarkan ke Circuit tersebut
examples.suggested: data yang di-broadcast (dipancarkan) ke Circuit tersebut
examples.why: 'Disiarkan' is the media or radio sense of broadcast. The array-broadcasting sense is better kept as a loanword or glossed.

examples.source: select the device you want to use
examples.translation: pilih peranti yang nak digunakan
examples.suggested: pilih peranti yang ingin anda gunakan
examples.why: 'Nak' is colloquial and a slip below the standard technical-documentation register. The same slip appears in [30].

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, including the Flex Plan caveats in [7] and [8], the 2x-minutes example in [11] and the FIFO logic in [14]. There are three small editorial issues. In [14], "oldest workload" became "beban kerja yang paling lama", which can also mean the workload that runs longest. The FIFO sentence right after it makes the meaning clear, but "yang paling awal dihantar" would remove the doubt. [6] has a stiff calque of the English relative clauses ("Konstruk peringkat asas yang kepadanya masa diperuntukkan ... dan yang kepadanya pengguna ditetapkan"), and [12] has the clumsy "akaun anak akaun tersebut".

examples.source: the scheduler will select the oldest workload first
examples.translation: penjadual akan memilih beban kerja yang paling lama terlebih dahulu
examples.suggested: penjadual akan memilih beban kerja yang paling awal dihantar terlebih dahulu
examples.why: 'paling lama' can mean either oldest or longest-running. The FIFO sentence after it makes the meaning clear, so this is minor, but the wording should be exact.

examples.source: The base-level construct to which time is allocated from the overarching account to a set of QPUs, and to which users are directly assigned.
examples.translation: Konstruk peringkat asas yang kepadanya masa diperuntukkan daripada akaun utama kepada satu set QPU, dan yang kepadanya pengguna ditetapkan secara langsung.
examples.suggested: Konstruk peringkat asas yang menerima peruntukan masa daripada akaun utama untuk satu set QPU, dan yang menjadi tempat pengguna ditetapkan secara langsung.
examples.why: This copies the English 'to which' clause structure word for word. A native writer would not repeat 'yang kepadanya'.

examples.source: distribute their allocations to the account's child accounts
examples.translation: mengedarkan peruntukan mereka kepada akaun anak akaun tersebut
examples.suggested: mengedarkan peruntukan mereka kepada akaun-akaun anak di bawahnya
examples.why: 'akaun anak akaun tersebut' repeats 'akaun' and is hard to read.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout, with correct IT terms: high availability is "ketersediaan tinggi", load balancer is "pengimbang beban", single point of failure is "titik kegagalan tunggal", and "tidak bertanggungjawab untuk perancangan atau tindakan pemulihan bencana" keeps the English meaning exactly.

The rewritten heading in entry 7, 'UNIX-like' → 'Seperti UNIX', has the right meaning and does not mislead. The problem is that the rest of the page still calls this section 'UNIX-like': 'sistem UNIX-like' in [8] and 'bahagian [UNIX-like](#unix)' in [27] and [80]. A reader sent to the 'UNIX-like' section will land on a heading with a different name. Also, 'Seperti UNIX' on its own is a prepositional phrase ('like UNIX'), so it reads stiffly as a heading. 'Sistem seakan-UNIX' would be more natural, or the heading could keep 'UNIX-like' to match the other entries.

examples.source: UNIX-like {#unix-like}
examples.translation: Seperti UNIX {#unix-like}
examples.suggested: Sistem seakan-UNIX {#unix-like}
examples.why: The heading no longer matches the name used for this section in [8], [27] and [80] ('UNIX-like'), so cross-references point to a heading with a different label. Also, 'Seperti UNIX' by itself is a prepositional phrase, not a natural section title. The meaning is correct, so this is a minor issue.

editor_note: The three rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. "Sistem pengendalian Tier 1:" and "Sistem pengendalian Tier 2:" (entries 50, 55) match the untranslated "Tier 1"/"Tier 2" accordion titles and the body text in entries 49 and 54, and "macOS ARM64 (11.0 atau lebih baharu)" (entry 52) keeps the version floor intact and matches "10.12 atau lebih baharu" in entry 56.

Rewritten entries 25 and 26 keep the meaning of the English, including the 28-day rolling window ("tetingkap penggunaan bergulir 28 hari"), the limited/not-limited conditions and the caveat that active work keeps running ("beban kerja yang aktif akan terus berjalan, termasuk beban kerja dalam mod Session"); entry 26 also spells "peruntukannya" correctly.

The translation is faithful throughout and I found nothing that would mislead a learner. The 50-qubit ceiling, the 15 May 2024 retirement date, the Open Plan caution and the note that local testing mode has no built-in error mitigation all come through intact. The clearest slip is in [31]: "noisy simulations" becomes "simulasi berhalangan" ("hindered/obstructed simulations"), which breaks the file's otherwise consistent noise→hingar convention and should be "simulasi berhingar". Two smaller wording issues are "custom" rendered as the loanword "kustom" in [28]/[34], where "tersuai" is the standard Malay, and "quantum utility" rendered as "kegunaan kuantum" in [3], which reads as plain "usefulness" rather than the established term "utiliti kuantum".

examples.source: useful for testing the transpiler and performing noisy simulations of the QPU
examples.translation: berguna untuk menguji Transpiler dan melakukan simulasi berhalangan QPU
examples.suggested: berguna untuk menguji Transpiler dan melakukan simulasi berhingar bagi QPU
examples.why: 'berhalangan' means hindered/obstructed, not noisy; the rest of the file uses 'hingar' for noise (model hingar, tanpa hingar).

examples.source: custom noise models
examples.translation: model hingar kustom
examples.suggested: model hingar tersuai
examples.why: 'tersuai' is the standard Malay (DBP) term for 'custom'; 'kustom' is an informal loan. The same applies in the table in [28].

examples.source: in this era of quantum utility
examples.translation: dalam era kegunaan kuantum ini
examples.suggested: dalam era utiliti kuantum ini
examples.why: 'Quantum utility' is IBM's name for a specific milestone; 'kegunaan' reads as generic usefulness and weakens the term.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful: "does break compatibility" becomes "tidak lagi serasi dengan semua versi Qiskit sebelumnya" in [3], and "Breaking package changes" becomes "Perubahan pakej Qiskit v1.0 yang tidak serasi ke belakang" in [6], which keeps the incompatibility caveat with nothing added or lost.

None of the three rewritten entries (70, 93, 101) changes the meaning: the code, the dropdown pointers and the accordion titles ("Panjang bacaan", "CLOPS (atau CLOPS_h)") all match the English. The problem is consistency. These entries translate IBM Quantum Platform UI section names that the rest of the page keeps in English, which is how they appear on the English-only platform: "Bahagian data penentukuran" (entry 70) against "Bahagian Calibration data", "Bahagian penentukuran" (entry 93) against "Bahagian Calibration", and "Bahagian Perincian" (entry 101) against "Bahagian Details". A learner looking for "Perincian" on the platform will not find it. The rewrites also use "Lihat pada IBM Quantum Platform" and a capitalized "menu lungsur Qubit", where the other rows say "Lihat di" and "menu lungsur qubit".

examples.line_approx: View on IBM Quantum Platform row
examples.source: Calibration data section: Qubit dropdown menu
examples.translation: Bahagian data penentukuran: menu lungsur Qubit
examples.suggested: Bahagian Calibration data: menu lungsur qubit
examples.why: The UI label is translated here, but the other rows on the page (e.g. entries 72, 88, 97) keep the English label that actually appears on IBM Quantum Platform.

examples.line_approx: View on IBM Quantum Platform row
examples.source: Calibration section: Qubit dropdown menu
examples.translation: Bahagian penentukuran: menu lungsur Qubit
examples.suggested: Bahagian Calibration: menu lungsur qubit
examples.why: The same row in entries 83 and 91 reads 'Bahagian Calibration'. Translating the UI section name makes it harder to find on the platform.

examples.line_approx: View on IBM Quantum Platform row
examples.source: Details section
examples.translation: Bahagian Perincian
examples.suggested: Bahagian Details
examples.why: Everywhere else on the page (entries 30, 43, 85, 90) the platform's 'Details' section keeps its English name. 'Perincian' does not match any label a learner will see in the UI.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The status list, the CPU/memory figures (16 cores, 32 GB, 2*1024^3 bytes) and the /data limitations all match the English. In [6], "compute accelerators" is rendered as "pempesat pengkomputeran". That is not a recognizable Malay word, and the usual term is "pemecut pengkomputeran". There are also two small calques a native editor would fix: "mengesahkan ke Qiskit Serverless" in [28] and "program yang dimuat naik anda" in [31]. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: including CPUs, QPUs, and other compute accelerators
examples.translation: termasuk CPU, QPU, dan pempesat pengkomputeran lain
examples.suggested: termasuk CPU, QPU, dan pemecut pengkomputeran lain
examples.why: 'pempesat' is not a standard Malay word; 'pemecut' is the conventional term for accelerator.

examples.source: Be sure you have authenticated to Qiskit Serverless with your IBM Quantum account
examples.translation: Pastikan anda telah mengesahkan ke Qiskit Serverless dengan akaun IBM Quantum anda
examples.suggested: Pastikan anda telah membuat pengesahan dengan Qiskit Serverless menggunakan akaun IBM Quantum anda
examples.why: 'mengesahkan ke' is a literal calque of 'authenticated to' and reads unnaturally.

examples.source: or your uploaded program
examples.translation: atau program yang dimuat naik anda
examples.suggested: atau program anda yang telah dimuat naik
examples.why: The possessive 'anda' is in the wrong place, which follows English word order; Malay puts it right after the noun.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: nothing drifts in the 2% depolarizing-per-CX setup, the (1 - p)^m decay reasoning or the 65% conservative-estimate caveat. Core terms are consistent: hingar for noise, boleh cerapan for observable, nilai jangkaan for expectation value, and pengurangan ralat for error mitigation. A native editor would still fix three things. Entry [10] switches from inclusive "kita" to exclusive "kami" for the same authorial "we" within one paragraph. Entry [16] calques "where n is" as "di mana $n$ adalah", when standard Malay would be "dengan $n$ ialah". Entries [6] and [16] also use "adalah" before noun predicates where "ialah" is the prescribed form.

examples.source: we need to specify explicit values for these parameters. In the next cell, we specify some values
examples.translation: kita perlu menentukan nilai eksplisit ... Dalam sel seterusnya, kami menentukan beberapa nilai
examples.suggested: kita perlu menentukan nilai eksplisit ... Dalam sel seterusnya, kita menentukan beberapa nilai
examples.why: The same authorial 'we' switches between inclusive kita and exclusive kami in one paragraph, which is inconsistent and awkward in a tutorial voice.

examples.source: where $n$ is the number of qubits, in this case, 2.
examples.translation: di mana $n$ adalah bilangan qubit, dalam kes ini, 2.
examples.suggested: dengan $n$ ialah bilangan qubit, iaitu 2 dalam kes ini.
examples.why: 'di mana' as a relative 'where' is an English calque. Malay technical writing uses 'dengan ... ialah' to define a variable.

examples.source: Qiskit Aer is a high-performance quantum circuit simulator
examples.translation: Qiskit Aer adalah simulator Circuit kuantum berprestasi tinggi
examples.suggested: Qiskit Aer ialah simulator litar kuantum berprestasi tinggi
examples.why: 'ialah' is the prescribed copula before a noun phrase. 'adalah' is a common but non-standard slip.

editor_note: Rewritten entry [7] "Plotkan histogram" is a faithful, natural Malay imperative heading that keeps "histogram" and fits the verb family "memplot" used in [15] and [23].

The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The asymptotic-optimality claim, the lower bound, amplitude amplification (penguatan amplitud) and the caveat on practical advantage all survive intact. Entry [4] has two word-choice slips. "square-root speed-up" becomes "peningkatan punca kuasa dua", which drops the idea of speed and clashes with "peningkatan kelajuan" two sentences later. "a variety of different settings" is calqued as "tetapan", a word that means configuration settings in Malay, when "situasi/konteks" is what the sentence means.

examples.source: the square-root speed-up that it offers
examples.translation: peningkatan punca kuasa dua yang ditawarkannya
examples.suggested: peningkatan kelajuan punca kuasa dua yang ditawarkannya
examples.why: Here 'speed-up' is rendered as the bare 'peningkatan' (improvement), while later in the same entry it is 'peningkatan kelajuan'. That is inconsistent, and the first rendering loses the idea of speed.

examples.source: can be obtained in a variety of different settings
examples.translation: boleh diperoleh dalam pelbagai tetapan yang berbeza
examples.suggested: boleh diperoleh dalam pelbagai situasi/konteks
examples.why: This is a calque. 'Tetapan' means configuration settings, but the source means problem contexts. 'Pelbagai ... yang berbeza' also says the same thing twice.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The exam prerequisite, the Credly notification and the privacy notice (data shared, subsidiaries and third parties, IBM privacy practices) all come through with no drift. There are some small wording issues. In [4], "Tamatkan kursus" (terminate/end the course) should be "Selesaikan kursus". The badge name is translated as "Asas Perniagaan Kuantum IBM", which won't match the English badge name learners see on Credly. Entries [6] and [11] use calques such as "dimaksudkan untuk diambil" and "dengan cara yang konsisten dengan".

examples.source: Complete the course to earn your IBM Quantum Business Foundations badge.
examples.translation: Tamatkan kursus untuk mendapatkan lencana Asas Perniagaan Kuantum IBM anda.
examples.suggested: Selesaikan kursus ini untuk mendapatkan lencana IBM Quantum Business Foundations anda.
examples.why: 'Tamatkan' means to end or terminate, not to complete successfully. The badge is a proper product name that appears in English on Credly, so translating it makes it harder to recognize.

examples.source: This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: Peperiksaan ini dimaksudkan untuk diambil selepas membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.suggested: Peperiksaan ini sepatutnya diambil selepas anda membaca pelajaran dalam kursus ini.
examples.why: 'dimaksudkan untuk diambil' is a word-for-word copy of the English passive and reads stiffly in Malay.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Ia akan dikendalikan dengan cara yang konsisten dengan amalan privasi IBM.
examples.suggested: Maklumat ini akan dikendalikan selaras dengan amalan privasi IBM.
examples.why: 'dengan cara yang konsisten dengan' copies the English structure; 'selaras dengan' is the idiomatic Malay phrase for formal notices.

editor_note: Entry 36 keeps the English meaning. It has the 0/1 limit for Estimator, 0 as no optimization and 1 as the default, the 0–3 range in other contexts, and the reason for optimization 0 plus skip_transpilation. The one weak spot is "pass manager", rendered as "pengurus lulus". Here "lulus" means passing an exam, so the phrase reads as an "exam-pass manager" instead of a manager of transpiler passes. It matches entry 25, so a learner can still follow it, but a native technical editor would keep "pass manager" in English or write "pengurus laluan (pass)".

examples.source: because we have already transpiled our circuit using the pass manager above
examples.translation: kerana kita telah mentranspil litar menggunakan pengurus lulus di atas
examples.suggested: kerana kita telah mentranspil litar menggunakan pass manager di atas
examples.why: 'lulus' is 'pass' in the sense of passing a test, not a transpiler pass. The phrase is a literal calque the field would keep in English. It is recognizable in context and consistent with entry 25, so it is minor.

editor_note: The course's subject, 'diagonalization', is rendered correctly only once, as 'pepenjuruan matriks' in [0]. Everywhere else it becomes 'penepatan' ([4] 'penepatan kuantum', [6] 'penepatan matriks', [11] badge name 'Algoritma penepatan kuantum'). 'Penepatan' means placement or fixing, so it names a different concept, and a learner reading the overview, audience and badge text would not know the course is about diagonalization. These three entries should read 'pepenjuruan'. A smaller point: 'variasi daripadanya' in [0] is stiff and would read better as 'variasinya'.

examples.source: This course provides an overview of several approaches to quantum diagonalization.
examples.translation: Kursus ini memberikan gambaran keseluruhan beberapa pendekatan untuk penepatan kuantum.
examples.suggested: Kursus ini memberikan gambaran keseluruhan tentang beberapa pendekatan untuk pepenjuruan kuantum.
examples.why: 'Penepatan' means placement or fixing, not diagonalization. It names the wrong concept and contradicts 'pepenjuruan' in [0].

examples.source: want to leverage its power in matrix diagonalization.
examples.translation: ingin memanfaatkan kuasanya dalam penepatan matriks.
examples.suggested: ingin memanfaatkan kuasanya dalam pepenjuruan matriks.
examples.why: 'Penepatan matriks' reads as 'matrix placement', which is not the linear-algebra operation the course teaches.

examples.source: To earn your badge for Quantum diagonalization algorithms
examples.translation: Untuk mendapatkan lencana Algoritma penepatan kuantum anda
examples.suggested: Untuk mendapatkan lencana Algoritma pepenjuruan kuantum anda
examples.why: The course and badge name carries the wrong term, so the course title no longer identifies its subject.

examples.source: including VQE, QKD, SKD and variations of these.
examples.translation: termasuk VQE, QKD, SKD dan variasi daripadanya.
examples.suggested: termasuk VQE, QKD, SKD serta variasinya.
examples.why: 'variasi daripadanya' is a stiff calque of 'variations of these'. 'variasinya' is the natural Malay form.

editor_note: The file renders "ground state" as both "keadaan dasar" ([10], [40], [49]) and "keadaan asas" ([20], [26], [34], [38], [53]), and it also uses "keadaan asas" for "basis states". In [53], "Anggaran tenaga keadaan asas melalui pensampelan keadaan asas Krylov" therefore reads as "ground-state energy via sampling Krylov ground states", which misstates what the method samples. "Diagonalization" is also split across "pepenjuruan/mempenjurukan" ([1], [4], [10]) and "penepatan/mentepati" ([5], [37], [56]); "mentepati" means "to fulfil/match exactly", not "to diagonalize". Smaller problems: "noise" is rendered as "bunyi" (acoustic sound) instead of "hingar" in [56], the text switches between "kita" and "kami", and "some overlap" becomes "sedikit pertindihan" ("a little overlap") in [26].

examples.source: Ground state energy estimations via sampling Krylov basis states
examples.translation: Anggaran tenaga keadaan asas melalui pensampelan keadaan asas Krylov
examples.suggested: Anggaran tenaga keadaan dasar melalui pensampelan keadaan basis Krylov
examples.why: The same phrase 'keadaan asas' is used for both ground state and basis state in one sentence, so the learner reads that Krylov ground states are sampled.

examples.source: To project and diagonalize the Hamiltonian
examples.translation: Untuk memproyeksikan dan mentepati Hamiltonian
examples.suggested: Untuk mengunjurkan dan mempenjurukan Hamiltonian
examples.why: 'mentepati' means 'fulfil/make exact', not 'diagonalize'. It conflicts with 'pepenjuruan' in the title and in [10]. 'memproyeksikan' also conflicts with 'mengunjurkan' in [10].

examples.source: Sample-based Krylov quantum diagonalization (SKQD)
examples.translation: penepatan kuantum Krylov berasaskan pensampelan (SKQD)
examples.suggested: pepenjuruan kuantum Krylov berasaskan pensampelan (SKQD)
examples.why: This is the method name, and it is rendered differently from the page title in [1] and [4].

examples.source: to effectively remove the effect of noise
examples.translation: untuk menghapuskan kesan bunyi secara berkesan
examples.suggested: untuk menghapuskan kesan hingar secara berkesan
examples.why: 'bunyi' means acoustic sound. Quantum noise is 'hingar'.

examples.source: a reference state that has some overlap with the ground state
examples.translation: yang mempunyai sedikit pertindihan dengan keadaan asas
examples.suggested: yang mempunyai pertindihan (bukan sifar) dengan keadaan dasar
examples.why: 'sedikit' means 'a little', which softens the requirement of non-negligible overlap. 'keadaan asas' here is also inconsistent with 'keadaan dasar' elsewhere.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful all the way through, and the exam, badge and Credly notice entries are accurate. Entry [4] has three wording slips that a native editor would fix. 'Mengandaikan kebiasaan dengan' reads as 'assumes a habit with'. Better: 'mengandaikan anda sudah agak biasa dengan', which also restores the dropped 'some'. 'Beberapa ulasan' gives 'review' the sense of commentary or critique, when the English means a recap. 'Boleh sesuai dengan aliran kerja' is a calque of 'fit into'. Separately, 'variational' is rendered 'variasi' (variation) instead of the usual 'variasional'. The term is still recognizable, so it does not mislead.

examples.source: but will also assume some familiarity with these methods
examples.translation: tetapi juga mengandaikan kebiasaan dengan kaedah-kaedah ini
examples.suggested: tetapi juga mengandaikan anda sudah agak biasa dengan kaedah-kaedah ini
examples.why: 'kebiasaan' mainly means habit or custom. The phrasing is odd, and it drops the qualifier 'some'.

examples.source: The course will offer some review of classical machine learning approaches ... how quantum computing can fit into existing machine learning workflows
examples.translation: Kursus ini akan menawarkan beberapa ulasan pendekatan pembelajaran mesin klasik ... boleh sesuai dengan aliran kerja pembelajaran mesin yang sedia ada
examples.suggested: Kursus ini akan mengimbas semula beberapa pendekatan pembelajaran mesin klasik ... boleh disepadukan ke dalam aliran kerja pembelajaran mesin sedia ada
examples.why: 'ulasan' means commentary, not a recap. 'boleh sesuai dengan' is a stiff calque of 'fit into'.

examples.source: variational quantum circuits
examples.translation: Circuit kuantum variasi
examples.suggested: litar kuantum variasional
examples.why: 'variasi' means 'variation'. The usual term for 'variational' is 'variasional'. It is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. None of the caveats, conditions or quantities drift, including the GHZ accidental-protection argument in [137]-[152]. The last third, however, switches to different terms from the first two thirds. 'Observable' is 'boleh cerap' in [110]/[112] but the non-standard 'boleh amat' in [141]/[149]. 'Fidelity' is 'ketepatan' ([47], [133] 'ketepatan Hellinger') but 'kesetiaan' from [141] on ([161] 'kesetiaan Hellinger'). 'Error suppression' is 'penyekatan ralat' until [168] turns it into 'penindasan ralat'. Other splits: 'lebih-putaran'/'putaran-lebih', 'Pauli twirling'/'twirling Pauli', 'ditranspil'/'ditranspilasi' and 'terbiar'/'diam'. Two smaller slips: in [47] 'isolated' is rendered 'disekat' (blocked) instead of 'diasingkan', and [52] doubles the ordinal ('ke-$j^{th}$').

editor_note: I checked every entry against the English and found no semantic drift. The truncation caveats, the 2^L growth, the limit of eight Pauli groups and the claim that noiseless results are exact all match the source. The terminology is the problem. "Noisy" appears as "berlingar", which means hovering or loitering, in [57] ("perkakasan berlingar") and [64] ("simulasi berlingar"), while the rest of the page uses "hingar"; it should be "berhingar". Backpropagation is rendered three ways: "pengundur-belakang", English "backpropagation", and "backpropagasi" (from [49] onward). "Unitary" is rendered as "kesatuan" ("union/unity") in [12], [14] and [15]; the usual term is "unitari". There are also calques: "kedua-dua nilai jangkaan bersetuju" ("the two values agree", [57]) and "Ideanya ialah" for "Ideally" ([60]).

editor_note: I found no meaning drift. The key technical claims are all rendered faithfully: the 10% bias band applies only to PEC+SLC, the overhead drops about 3.4-fold, timeouts give the trivial bound of 2, and shades are upper bounds that never underestimate. The problem is inconsistent terminology. 'bound' is usually 'sempadan' but becomes 'batas' in [67], [73] and [86]. 'bias' turns into 'pincang' in [137]. 'lightcone shading' appears as 'pelorekan kon cahaya' in [72], 'Pembayangan lightcone' in [155] and plain 'lightcone shading' in [150]. 'mitigation' switches between 'mitigasi' and 'pengurangan', and 'overhed' sits alongside 'overhead'. Some entries were left in English: [37] 'Requirements', [44] 'Setup' and the whole heading at [144]. A few phrases read awkwardly: [84] is garbled, [73] uses 'pekerjaan' for a job, and [7] slips into casual 'kamu'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: the 6^num_reps overhead, the ideal values -1/+1, the Hadamard basis-change example and the no-mitigation caveat all survive. editor_note: I found no semantic drift. The caveat in [51] is kept intact: longer chains leave less freedom, so updated data matters less ("menjadi kurang substansial"). T1, T2, SPAM and RB are also explained faithfully. In [45], "fitting routine cannot fit a curve" is calqued as "rutin pemasangan tidak dapat memasang lengkung". In Malay, "pemasangan/memasang" reads as installation or assembly. The usual term for curve fitting is "penyuaian lengkung" ("rutin penyuaian ... tidak dapat menyuaikan lengkung"). The register also switches: the body uses casual "kamu" ([6], [9], [37], [45], [53]), but the call-to-action admonition in [51] switches to "anda". The house convention is "anda" throughout.

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout. The caveats that matter are kept: two-qubit errors sit higher, T2 sits lower, the difference comes from methodology rather than drift, and the refresh stays local to your session. There are a few wrong-sense words. "Pulse train" / "dynamical decoupling train" is rendered "latihan" (training) in [84] and [85], "streamlined" is rendered "teragih" (distributed) in [17], "relax" is rendered "berehat" (to rest) in [44], and "pass" is rendered as the non-word "laluk" in [49] and [70]. Terminology also drifts within the file: properties are "ciri"/"sifat", gate is "get"/"gate", job is "tugasan"/"job"/"pekerjaan", calibration is "kalibrasi"/"penentukuran", benchmarking is "penanda arasan"/"penanda aras", and survival probability is "kelangsungan"/"kemandirian".

examples.why: 'berehat' (to take a rest) is a literal calque. Elsewhere the file uses 'relaksasi'.

examples.source: You can pass any subset of the following experiments
examples.translation: Anda boleh laluk mana-mana subset eksperimen berikut
examples.suggested: Anda boleh menghantar mana-mana subset eksperimen berikut
examples.why: 'laluk' is not a Malay word. The same error appears in [70].

examples.source: submits multiple jobs
examples.translation: menghantar berbilang job
examples.suggested: Use one term consistently (e.g. 'job' or 'tugasan')
examples.why: Job is rendered 'tugasan' in [17] and [33], 'job' here and in [57]–[65], and 'pekerjaan' in [91]. Calibration and properties also switch between two renderings each.

editor_note: Nothing here would mislead a learner. The translation keeps the meaning throughout, including the lifecycle table, the Slurm/SPANK injection explanation and the accuracy caveat in [75] (23.7 kcal/mol above the reference, no chemical accuracy). Three word choices are worth fixing. In [76], "opposite-spin interactions" becomes "interaksi putaran bertentangan", which reads as rotation, while [72] keeps "spin-orbital". In [24], "composable" becomes "boleh disusun semula" ("re-arrangeable"). In [45], "standalone execution" becomes "pelaksanaan berdikari", a word normally used for self-reliant people.

examples.source: removed the opposite-spin interactions `(24, 24)` and `(20, 20)`
examples.translation: mengalih keluar interaksi putaran bertentangan
examples.suggested: mengalih keluar interaksi spin bertentangan
examples.why: 'Putaran' means rotation, not quantum spin. It also clashes with 'spin-orbital' in [72], so a learner could read this as rotational interactions.

examples.source: This keeps the interface minimal and composable.
examples.translation: Ini mengekalkan antara muka yang minimum dan boleh disusun semula.
examples.suggested: Ini memastikan antara muka kekal minimum dan boleh digabungkan dengan komponen lain.
examples.why: 'Composable' means it can be combined with other components. 'Boleh disusun semula' means it can be rearranged, which shifts the design point slightly.

examples.source: For standalone execution, create a `.env` file
examples.translation: Untuk pelaksanaan berdikari, cipta fail `.env`
examples.suggested: Untuk pelaksanaan secara kendiri (tanpa Slurm), cipta fail `.env`
examples.why: 'Berdikari' describes self-reliant people and sounds odd for running software on its own. 'Kendiri' is the usual technical word.

editor_note: In [17], "falsifiable test" becomes "ujian ... boleh dipalsukan", which means "a test that can be faked or forged". That turns a strength of the method into a claim about fraud, so it would mislead a learner. "Mitigated execution" is rendered as "pelaksanaan yang dikurangkan" ("reduced execution") in [11], [24] and [27], while later entries use "mitigasi ralat". "Deploy" is rendered as "gunakan/digunakan" ("use") in [0], [6] and [30], so the step "deploy the function template first" reads as "use the function template first". There are also smaller slips: "resolved" (spectral resolution) becomes "diselesaikan" ("solved") in [49] and [68]; the kick is called ketuk/ketukan/tendangan; fidelity is both kesetiaan and fideliti; and "dashed curves" is "lengkung bertitik" (dotted) in [17] but "bergaris putus" in [68].

examples.source: is a direct, falsifiable test of a quantum simulation
examples.translation: adalah ujian langsung dan boleh dipalsukan bagi simulasi kuantum
examples.suggested: adalah ujian langsung yang boleh disangkal (boleh diuji kepalsuannya) bagi simulasi kuantum
examples.why: 'dipalsukan' means forged or counterfeited. The sentence now says the test can be faked, not that it can be proven wrong.

examples.source: and mitigated execution as a single function call
examples.translation: dan pelaksanaan yang dikurangkan sebagai satu panggilan fungsi sahaja
examples.suggested: dan pelaksanaan dengan mitigasi ralat sebagai satu panggilan fungsi sahaja
examples.why: 'dikurangkan' means reduced. It suggests the execution itself is cut down rather than error-mitigated. The same wording appears in [24] and [27], while [46] and [59] use 'mitigasi ralat'.

examples.source: You must first [deploy the function template]
examples.translation: Anda mesti terlebih dahulu [menggunakan templat fungsi]
examples.suggested: Anda mesti terlebih dahulu [mengerahkan (deploy) templat fungsi]
examples.why: 'menggunakan' means 'use', so the deployment prerequisite is hidden. The same problem appears in [0] and [30] ('Gunakan dan jalankan').

examples.source: the two-spinon continuum is only coarsely resolved
examples.translation: kontinum dwi-spinon hanya diselesaikan secara kasar
examples.suggested: kontinum dua-spinon hanya dileraikan (resolusi) secara kasar
examples.why: 'diselesaikan' means solved, not spectrally resolved. The same appears in [68]. Also, 'dua-spinon' in [12]/[17] becomes 'dwi-spinon' here.

examples.source: then bake in the neutron kick
examples.translation: kemudian masukkan tendangan neutron
examples.suggested: use one term for 'kick' throughout, e.g. 'ketukan neutron'
examples.why: 'Kick' is rendered as ketuk [20], ketukan [25]/[27] and tendangan [44]/[47]/[56]. Fidelity is likewise split between kesetiaan and fideliti.

editor_note: Entry 7 is faithful and reads naturally: "tenaga keadaan asas" (ground-state energy), "sebutan kubik" (cubic terms) and "pengoptimuman binari peringkat tinggi (HOBO)" are correct and match entry 1, and the three application examples are all kept.
